source.note: MusicXML specifies source pitch step+alter+octave and transpose diatonic+chromatic; predicates and two-valued intervals below are SENS research proposals derived from this model, not claimed existing MusicXML APIs.

scope.pitch_model: MIDI-compatible 12 equal-tempered semitone numbers; retain MusicXML distinct diatonic spelling
exclude: keys/tonality context or transposing instruments without explicit written-to-sounding policy
MIDI routing, devices, host audio effects
scope.representation: (step, integer chromatic alter, octave), not a MIDI packet

candidates.semantic_law: Given two valid 12-TET MusicXML-like pitches (step, integer alter, octave), return 1 iff their exact sounding semitone index matches AND their notation triple differs; otherwise 0. An equal note written identically is not an enharmonic respelling.

positive_witnesses.explanation: C-sharp and D-flat agree in sounding semitones
double flat is distinct notation with same sound

falsifiers.explanation: octave is audible; pitch class alone insufficient

candidates.dedup_attack: Different from MODULO, EQ, EQUAL and raw MIDI pitch equality: predicate requires BOTH equality under 12-TET sounding projection AND inequality of preserved diatonic spelling. Explicit D1-D9 behavioral review required before SELECT, not established solely by name search.
candidates.dependency: Derived from exact integer addition and equality; derivability alone not an exclusion under #4013. Distinct two-identity observation needs owner review.
attacks: Two identical pitch triples MUST yield 0, not 1
Enharmonic equality must not be inferred from pitch class modulo 12 alone
No claim for just intonation or microtones

candidates.result_cardinality: two exact signed integers (diatonic steps, chromatic semitones)
candidates.semantic_law: Given two valid pitches, return ordered signed pair (target octave*7+step ordinal minus source octave*7+step ordinal, target exact 12-TET semitone number minus source semitone number); neither component may be silently discarded.

positive_witnesses.explanation: major third, two notated diatonic steps
F-flat and E natural have same sounding semitone distance but DIFFERENT diatonic interval
the sounding note is same yet one written step apart

falsifiers.explanation: diatonic steps are not semitone count
do not erase spelling via MIDI pitch projection
enharmonic change still one diatonic step

candidates.dedup_attack: Not ordinary pitch subtraction and not two aliases of SUB/MOD: the semitone result alone cannot recover the exact notated diatonic distance, so the two-component observable remains distinct from a single scalar. Behavioral dedup against D1-D9 / selected D10 still mandatory.
candidates.dependency: Exact diatonic ordinal and 12-TET semitone projection; two outputs may be implemented using existing arithmetic, but that does not collapse the observable law.
attacks: C→E and C→F-flat must NOT return identical two-component results
Notation-aware negative intervals must be antisymmetric
Host MIDI opcode and audio synthesis are not language-owned laws

reviewer_gates: Confirm no behavioral duplicates in all owner-ratified D1–D9, not name-only
Compare against full current D10 semantic inventory and concurrent PRs
Execute a real external independent MusicXML importer/conformer for source-to-representation cases
Decide whether each composed law deserves one D10 resident or a library derived definition
Never assign coordinates, ratify or change the 631 selected census before explicit owner review

relation_to_other_work.benefit: Score-oriented symbolic music and exact note semantics; same source-independent integer law may be tested for acoustic analyzers, FPGA pitch-display frontends and music theory libraries, without declaring any hardware backend a new resident.
